absent: Internal layouts and semantics of the aggregator core types and world and key records referenced but not defined in these fragments.
Executable behavior of creation, lookup, release, statistics, and hints operations of the aggregator core.
Behavior of world helpers and root and delta lifecycle callbacks referenced but not shown.
Numeric value of the total key population and meaning of the greedy selection option beyond its name.
Locking, concurrency, and lifetime rules for aggregator objects, statistics snapshots, and hints objects.
Threading, timing, and synchronization use of the pool test runtime state beyond static field composition.
Module registration, build selection, and initialization ordering for the test modules.

findings.text: A compact accounting record holds two atomically updated long tallies, the allocation role named alloc and the release role named free, separating allocation events from release events for one allocator path.
A small outcome record holds two plain unsigned long counters, the hit role named nhits and the miss role named nmiss, summarizing object lookup results.

Runtime state for the pool test combines gated start control with staged waiting, worker accounting, allocator accounting, object accounting, and elapsed time. Start control uses a read write semaphore member named start. Staged waiting uses two completion members named wait and rcu. Worker accounting uses two cacheline separated atomics named nthreads and stop. Allocator accounting reuses the long tally record for members named kmalloc and vmalloc. Object accounting reuses the hit record for a member named objects. Elapsed time is a sixty four bit value named duration.

Test configuration couples execution selectors with sizing and timing parameters plus a name and embedded runtime state. Selectors include an async flag named async and a mode value named mode that only supports zero. Sizing includes object size named objsz and two bulk depths named bulk_normal and bulk_irq. Timing includes run length named duration, pacing gap named delay, and timer period named hrtimer. Identity is a string pointer named name and live state is an embedded record named data.
The upper bound for bulk handling in the pool test named OT_NR_MAX_BULK is sixteen.

An expected per object snapshot pairs usage tallies with placement and identity. Usage is a statistics record named stats. Placement is a boolean flag named is_root distinguishing root entries from delta entries. Identity is an unsigned key value named key_id.

An expected collection snapshot holds a total length plus a fixed capacity array of per object snapshots. Length is named info_count and storage is named info with capacity tied to the overall key population defined outside these fragments.

A scripted step record binds one key operation to its expected counter movements and resulting collection snapshot. The affected key is named key_id, the operation selector is named action, the delta movement selector is named expect_delta, the root movement selector is named expect_root, and the resulting snapshot is named expect_stats.

A hints scenario record references a key replay sequence and two collection snapshots. The sequence pointer is named key_ids with length named key_ids_count, the baseline snapshot is named expect_stats, and the hint optimized snapshot is named expect_stats_hints.

Scripted operations use three small selectors. The operation selector named action offers acquisition named ACTION_GET and release named ACTION_PUT. The delta movement selector named expect_delta offers unchanged, incremented, and decremented alternatives. The root movement selector named expect_root offers the same three movement alternatives.

Three helpers build expected snapshots without manual structure literals. The collection helper named EXPECT_STATS assembles a snapshot from a length and entry list. The root helper named ROOT marks a root entry from a key plus direct and delta tallies. The delta helper named DELTA marks a delta entry from a key plus a shared tally.

Two operation tables named nodelta_ops and delta_ops share test key sizing and root lifecycle handling while differing in delta handling. The no delta table always declines delta reuse, always fails delta creation as unsupported, and does nothing on delta teardown. The delta table delegates to separately defined delta handlers that are exercised by the scripted suite.

Acquisition validation in the no delta suite randomizes the pending root buffer only when creation is expected, then fetches the object and checks that the global root tally moved exactly as expected, that the stored key matches the requested key, and that stored content matches the pending buffer when creation was expected. Any mismatch releases the reference and reports an invalid argument outcome.

Release validation in the no delta suite drops the reference and then checks that the global root tally either stepped down or stayed put exactly as the expectation flag requires, reporting an invalid argument outcome on mismatch.
Empty state expects zero collected entries. Populated no delta state expects one entry per key in the population, with each entry showing two direct users and two delta users.

The no delta suite runs an empty check, a creation pass over the key space, a reuse pass that must create nothing new, a populated statistics check, two reverse release passes that first retain roots and then destroy them, a final empty check, and teardown. Failures unwind by releasing already acquired keys before teardown.

Counter verification compares live delta and root tallies against unchanged, incremented, or decremented expectations. Increment expectations are rejected for release steps and decrement expectations are rejected for acquisition steps as programming errors.
Effective key resolution reads the identifier stored in root private data and, only when delta private data is present, adds a stored difference to obtain the delta key.

Statistics verification requires exact total length match and then per position agreement on placement flag and both user tallies plus key identity. When the key at a position mismatches but numbers agree, verification searches neighboring entries with matching numbers for the expected key before failing. Snapshot acquisition failures and mismatches are reported with diagnostic text and the snapshot is always released.

Each scripted delta step records starting tallies, performs one acquisition or release, and unless it is an unwind repetition, verifies counter movements and the full expected snapshot. A verification failure triggers one compensating opposite operation to restore state. The suite walks the whole scripted table and on failure unwinds completed steps in reverse with compensating operations before teardown.

The hints scenario replays a twelve element key sequence and defines two full snapshots over the same population. The baseline snapshot and the hint optimized snapshot differ in which keys become roots and how deltas attach, capturing the effect of greedy root selection.

The hints suite builds one aggregator without hints, replays the fixed sequence, validates the baseline snapshot, derives a hints object with simple greedy selection, then builds a second aggregator using those hints, replays the same sequence, and requires the hint optimized snapshot both from the hints object and the second aggregator. Debug dumps surround major stages and failures unwind all acquired keys before teardown.

Root and delta objects follow a reference counted lifecycle driven by acquisitions and releases. First use of a key family creates a root. Compatible later keys create deltas attached to an existing root instead of new roots. Repeated acquisition of an existing key only raises tallies. A root with no direct users persists while deltas reference it and disappears with its last delta. Full release of all keys returns the system to empty.
Module initialization runs the no delta suite, then the delta suite, then the hints suite, stopping at the first failure and propagating its status. Module teardown performs no work.

Callers must release every acquired object and every statistics or hints snapshot, including on verification failure paths that unwind with compensating operations, or references and snapshots leak. Unwind repetitions must skip verification to avoid recursive compensation. Buffer comparison is meaningful only when root creation was expected.
